title: SIP Load and Re-Invite
scope: Historical Cisco VoIP mailing-list post dated 2011-04-15; product context: CUCM before 8.5 is explicitly discussed; no complete deployed version matrix is stated.
observation: Technical explanation in a list discussion, including a cited release-note description; not a controlled reproduction report. A participant explains that hold/resume and supplementary call operations could leave media inactive when a third-party endpoint returned an inactive SDP answer where the older call flow expected send/receive media. The thread also discusses the changed behavior in CUCM 8.5. Outcome noted in the thread: Historical version-dependent interoperability behavior is described; no specific customer call is confirmed as repaired in this thread.
requirement: Candidate observable behavior: When both endpoint profiles accept the negotiated resume offer, signalling and both media directions recover after hold/resume. Negative boundary: When the far endpoint returns an incompatible inactive answer, retain successful signalling but report the affected media leg as inactive and identify the profile interaction; do not claim the historical version behavior is universal. Pending mechanisms: The calling pack reports codec, encryption, NAT and quality dimensions. The core can show signalling success with failed media, but does not model hold/resume SDP negotiation or endpoint-specific offer/answer contracts. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:media, uc-new:domain:signalling.
uncertainty: Applies to the described historical offer/answer behavior and counterpart implementations; not a general claim about current SIP endpoints. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.

title: quick question about sip and CUBE

The thread explains that trunk ingress node membership and dial-peer node preference must align; changing preference resolved calls for the reporter. Outcome noted in the thread: The reporter states that reversing publisher/subscriber dial-peer preference made calls work; the discussion also points to all-node trunk operation in later versions.
requirement: Candidate observable behavior: A request arriving at an allowed trunk node matches the configured service and proceeds to dial-plan evaluation. Negative boundary: A request delivered to a disallowed node returns a synthetic device-handler rejection even when the destination number is valid; adjusting preference or enabling a supported all-node mode repairs only after provisioning. Pending mechanisms: The foundation has generic trunk readiness and route matching but does not model ingress-node membership, cluster call-manager groups or SIP device-handler matching. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:signalling, uc-new:domain:directory-dialplan, uc-new:domain:provisioning.
uncertainty: This is a historical cluster/trunk routing example, not a claim that all 503 responses have this cause. Historical anecdote or technical discussion only; not current vendor behavior, support policy, or a general product rule.

Outcome noted in the thread: The follow-up reports successful phone registration after trust-chain handling; it is not a statement of current recommended certificate operations.

Pending mechanisms: The core has generic certificates and external connectivity dependencies but not per-endpoint trust roots, activation-code enrollment or separate client-versus-phone MRA capability. Candidate source: uc-new:domain:provisioning, uc-new:domain:signalling, uc-new:family:cisco:dedicated-premises.
